recommendation: Keep the audit commit and ask FHIR-I to decide whether history Bundle entries may use entry.request.method PATCH. If yes, revise bdl-14 and the HTTP history section; if no, remove PATCH from the Bundle history resource-inclusion sentence and align bdl-3b/profile wording with the PUT-as-history representation.
issue_request: FHIR-34388 is Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested changing the Bundle history sentence from requiring a resource for PUT or POST history entries to requiring a resource for PUT, PATCH or POST entries.
initial_application: Commit 27121ee5c4bca5fb4eae4bc20fff012202eea5ce explicitly applied FHIR-34388 by adding PATCH to source/bundle/bundle-notes.xml. The Bundle resource is active in source/fhir.ini, so that narrative is in current build scope.
additional_context: FHIR-19620 is also Published/Persuasive and more specifically decided that PATCH interactions create history entries but are represented as PUT in history Bundles, with an invariant prohibiting entry.request.method PATCH when Bundle.type is history. Current source still contains bdl-14 and HTTP history text that implement FHIR-19620. The originating FHIR-19620 Zulip discussion supports PUT representation, while FHIR-34388's later Zulip thread and FHIR-I minutes support the narrower wording change. FHIR-50118 is a later Triaged issue about bdl-3b text/expression mismatch, but it is unresolved and does not settle PATCH semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source is not safe to edit automatically because the two Published decisions lead to opposite conformance outcomes: either allow PATCH in history Bundles and remove/revise bdl-14 and HTTP guidance, or keep PATCH represented as PUT and remove PATCH from the Bundle history resource-inclusion sentence.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive decision says PATCH creates history but is represented as PUT and adds an invariant forbidding PATCH in history Bundles.
Later Triaged issue reports a bdl-3b text/expression mismatch but is unresolved and does not decide PATCH history semantics.
Earlier Published issue added PATCH to the Bundle.entry.request.method value set generally, explaining PATCH availability in transaction and batch contexts.
